artifact.title: SporeApp managers, service singletons, registries, pools, and lookup containers
artifact.purpose: Read-only clean-room archaeology of original manager access patterns, collection layouts, lifecycle boundaries, ownership evidence, and replaceable contracts.

major_claims.claim: The SDK export contains 66 exact ::Get anchors, but only a subset are direct reads from stable global service slots; the rest use indirect, factory-derived, mode-derived, thread-local, or unresolved access paths.

The 00b3d220-00b3d5a0 region is a mixed simulator service-accessor family containing named SDK anchors, unnamed six-byte accessors, longer factory or mode-derived functions, and SDK anchors absorbed into neighboring bodies.
The simulator root vector at cSimulatorSystem+0x5c owns intrusive ISimulatorStrategy references and is the principal manager composition boundary.
Manager responsibility is exposed through several distinct container shapes: intrusive vectors and lists, EASTL vectors, hash maps, ordered maps, nested vectors, and fixed-pool allocators.
The main Cell pool is a 4096-element, 920-byte-element free-list pool embedded behind cCellGame state, and its first object word doubles as free-list link and allocated object index.

Global accessors, original vtable ABIs, EASTL layouts, allocator internals, RenderWare and Direct3D dependencies, and the original global spine are replaceable boundaries; semantic identity, ordering, ownership, handles, and lifecycle remain compatibility contracts.

stage_singleton_families.description: Application, graphics, message, cheat, property, and locale service spine with stable four-byte slots and direct SDK accessors.
Simulator service spine containing documented direct slots, unresolved gaps, and named managers whose slots are not ordered by their accessor addresses.
Mixed six-byte and longer simulator accessors. Exact SDK anchors are sparse; unnamed gaps and absorbed anchors prevent treating the range as a clean 16-slot table.
Ten contiguous editor-stage pointer candidates. Their exact manager identities and lifecycle ownership are not established by the available pinned records.

pools_and_allocators.element_link_contract: The first object word stores the next free index while free and the object's own index while allocated.
pools_and_allocators.ownership: Embedded in Cell-stage state at sCellGame+0x1c; the evidence supports stage ownership, not process-lifetime ownership.

lifecycle_boundaries.sequence: The application bootstrap establishes the application service spine before stage-specific managers are consumed.
IGameMode implementations are registered in App::cGameModeManager::mEntries; switching selects by active index and drives mode enter or exit callbacks.
cSimulatorSystem owns intrusive simulator strategies; consumers reach individual services through the mixed accessor family.
Listeners are stored by message ID in cMessageManager and are mutated or dispatched under a listener mutex.
Cell-stage initialization establishes the main pool and query candidates; disposal releases stage resources and resets global stage pointers.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: Global four-byte service slots with SDK Get wrappers.
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Inject typed service references or a composition root with explicit startup and shutdown ordering.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: Intrusive ISimulatorStrategy vector owned by cSimulatorSystem.
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Use an explicit typed strategy registry with deterministic ordering and scoped ownership.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: App::cGameModeManager stores intrusive IGameMode entries and an active index.
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Use an explicit GameMode interface and GameModeManager owned by the application composition root.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: Manager-specific maps, vectors, lists, and mutexes.
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Use standard C++ typed registries with explicit ownership and concurrency contracts.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: cResourceManager combines factories, type maps, cache, allocators, notification maps, and mutexes.
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Use a typed IResourceProvider seam keyed by type, group, and instance.

ownership_and_replaceability.original_boundary: cObjectPool free-list layout and Cell-stage global ownership.
replace: raw object layout outside observed fields
ownership_and_replaceability.clean_room_direction: Own a typed CellPool inside CellGame and expose stable handles rather than global access.

conflicts.historical_claim: A prior campaign described a complete set of 15 or 16 managers.
conflicts.current_evidence: The SDK inventory, named slots, unnamed gaps, and factory-derived accessors do not form that bounded set.
conflicts.resolution: Retain the historical count only as a superseded campaign summary; use the classified accessor and slot inventory in this artifact.

conflicts.historical_claim: The 00b3d240-00b3d5a0 region can be read as a uniform sequence of global service getters.
conflicts.current_evidence: The region contains unnamed six-byte functions, non-global longer bodies, and SDK anchors absorbed into neighboring function boundaries.
conflicts.resolution: Treat it as a mixed accessor family, not a table whose address order defines slot order.

conflicts.historical_claim: 0x00b3d2a0 was labeled as a player ID accessor.
conflicts.current_evidence: Its consumers are mixed and do not establish one stable player identity abstraction.
conflicts.resolution: Keep the function unnamed pending direct data-flow characterization.

conflicts.current_evidence: Materialized noun-map behavior provides a competing semantic explanation.
conflicts.resolution: Keep the label withdrawn; separate noun materialization from message registration.

conflicts.historical_claim: A mode-entry vector was attributed to Simulator::cGameModeManager+0x14.
conflicts.current_evidence: The vector with mode pointer, ID, and name is App::cGameModeManager+0x14; Simulator::cGameModeManager+0x14 is an unnamed state field in the SDK layout.
conflicts.resolution: Namespace and type-qualify all mode-registry claims.

conflicts.historical_claim: Decompiled return and field types are exact original types.
conflicts.current_evidence: The committed SDK structures and imported fields disagree with several decompiler names and inferred types.
conflicts.resolution: Use direct offsets and operations for mechanics; preserve SDK provenance separately from decompiler inference.

current_openspore_comparison.original_fact: A 28-byte manager stores a preallocated object array, free-list head, pool identifier, capacity, live count, element size, and trailing state.
current_openspore_comparison.openspore_fact: src/sim/CellPool.hpp models the 28-byte manager and 920-byte Cell object, uses the first word as free-list link or self index, and exposes typed allocation and indexed access.
current_openspore_comparison.difference: The clean-room pool is owned by typed CellGame state rather than the original global stage spine.

current_openspore_comparison.original_fact: App::cGameModeManager stores intrusive IGameMode entries with ID, name, and active index.
current_openspore_comparison.openspore_fact: src/apps/CellModeStrategy.hpp uses an IGameMode vector, explicit active index, and CellModeStrategy-owned CellGfx and CellUI resources.
current_openspore_comparison.difference: The original vtable ABI and global access are replaced by a smaller clean-room interface and scoped ownership.

current_openspore_comparison.original_fact: cResourceManager combines factory, type, cache, allocator, notification, and synchronization state behind a 38-slot interface.
current_openspore_comparison.openspore_fact: src/compat/ResourceProvider.hpp exposes fetch by type, group, and instance and provides DBPF and in-memory providers.
current_openspore_comparison.difference: The current seam preserves identity and lookup semantics while replacing the original manager ABI and backend coupling.
